latest_session.title: 2026-09-18 (evening)
latest_session.goal: Explain and fix the Windows Update prompt that appears at every boot ("Intel - Extension - 2.1.10103.24"), left open from the crash-diagnosis sessions.
latest_session.outcome: Loop mechanism identified from `C:\Windows\INF\setupapi.dev.log` (11 rounds since 09-11). Each "OK" install stages `ipf_ef_ext.inf` (Intel IPF Extensible Framework Extension) as `oem337.inf`, PnP lists it as Selected for the IPF device `PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_7D03` but cannot bind its install section against base driver `ipf_cpu.inf` 2.3.20300.4905 (installed by HP/WU on 09-14), configures the device with only `oem321`+`oem211`+`oem314`, then deletes the unreferenced package 40 s later (`Delete flags 0x2`). WU records exit 0, the device still lacks extension ID `{002c4697-...}`, and the package is re-offered at the next scan. The package therefore never appears in the PnP driver inventory. It is an Intel/HP catalog mismatch, harmless; hiding the package is the fix. Also observed: the machine has not been rebooted since the 16:04 crash (`PendingFileRenameOperations` set), so the post-Cisco reboot is still outstanding. Six other driver updates queued (Realtek, HP keyboard/software component, Cirrus Logic, Logitech) are one-shot, not part of the loop.
latest_session.next_steps: User runs `hide_intel_ext.ps1` from the admin prompt, then reboots. Machine watch and IT mail as in the previous session. Infrastructure backlog unchanged, see `_state/current.md`.
